title: Fried Brussels Sprouts with Crisp Shallots, Honey and Balsamic
summary: Deep-fried Brussels sprouts and shallots tossed in a sweet honey and balsamic dressing with fresh parsley, for a crisp, punchy side.

ingredients.item: Brussels sprouts, trimmed, outer leaves removed, halved
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dressing
steps.text: Mix 3 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar and the chopped parsley in a small bowl.

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Heat the oil in a wok to 205°C.

steps.title: First batch
steps.text: Fry half the sprouts and half the shallots, letting the oil fall to about 165°C and holding it there, stirring until deep golden brown, about 4 min.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Lift the sprouts and shallots onto kitchen paper.

steps.title: Second batch
steps.text: Reheat the oil to 205°C and fry the remaining sprouts and shallots.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Tip the hot sprouts and shallots into a bowl with the dressing, toss, season with ¾ tsp salt and ¼ tsp pepper and serve at once.

tips: Make sure the sprouts are completely dry before frying, as any moisture will cause the oil to spatter.
Fry in two batches and keep the oil at the right temperature so the sprouts crisp rather than steam.
Toss the sprouts in the dressing as soon as they're drained, while they're still hot.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best served immediately while crisp; leftovers can be kept covered in the fridge for a day but will soften on reheating. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
